scope: US federal programs where the government pays or guarantees rent to private landlords, and the open data showing which homes qualify and for how much. Licence and access tested by script.
licence_basis_default: Works of the US federal government are not subject to US copyright (17 U.S.C. 105). Agency-specific terms recorded where they add conditions.

sources.name: SAFMR designated (mandatory) metro areas with 90%/110% payment-standard bands
sources.what: ZIP polygons in the 61 metros where Small Area FMRs are mandatory for HCV payment standards (designated 2018 or 2024), with SAFMR by bedroom plus precomputed 90% and 110% values.

licence.phrase: HUD eGIS open data (federal work, public domain)

sources.tested: yes: 6,884 ZIP features; distinct Metro_Name/Year_Designated returned (e.g. Atlanta 2018, Los Angeles 2024, Seattle 2024). Layer last edited Nov 2024, so its dollar fields may be a prior FY. Use it for the mandatory flag and take dollars from the current SAFMR file (already integrated).
sources.how_to_use_per_house: Point-in-polygon. Inside: PHA payment standards must come from the ZIP SAFMR, so voucher ceiling = SAFMR(ZIP, bedrooms) x 0.90 to 1.10 (PHA chooses). Outside: metro/county FMR x 0.90 to 1.10, unless the PHA opted in to SAFMR.
sources.update_frequency: designations by Federal Register notice (2016, 2023); SAFMR dollars annual (Oct 1)

sources.name: Housing Choice Vouchers by tract
sources.what: Voucher households per tract and % of renter units with a voucher.

licence.phrase: HUD eGIS open data (federal work, public domain)

sources.tested: yes: point query Atlanta (-84.39,33.75) -> tract 13121003500, HCV_PUBLIC=34, HCV_PUBLIC_PCT=4
sources.how_to_use_per_house: Demand signal: many vouchers = proven voucher market with an existing PHA landlord base. 0% may mean rents above the payment standard.

sources.name: Picture of Subsidized Households 2025 (2020-census geography)
sources.what: Units, % occupied, average household rent contribution, HUD spending per unit, income, waiting time and more, by program (HCV, project-based Section 8, public housing, 202/811, mod rehab), for US/state/CBSA/county/place/tract/ZIP/PHA/project.
sources.geography: tract, ZIP, PHA, project, county, place, CD
sources.access: https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/assthsg.html ; e.g. https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/pictures/files/Zipcode_2025_2020census.xlsx (47 MB), TRACT_AK_MN_2025_2020census.xlsx, TRACT_MO_WY_2025_2020census.xlsx, PHA_2025_2020census.xlsx; dictionary https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/pictures/dictionary_2025.pdf
sources.key_required: no for files; the Picture API (https://www.huduser.gov/portal/dataset/picture-api.html) uses a free HUD User token

licence.phrase: Federal work. If the HUD User API is used, show: 'This product uses the HUD User Data API but is not endorsed or certified by HUD User'

sources.tested: yes: range request on Zipcode_2025_2020census.xlsx -> 206, xlsx, 47,481,265 bytes. The eGIS 'Snapshot' layer is older (2019 ACS, edited 2022), so prefer the 2025 files.
sources.how_to_use_per_house: ZIP/tract row for 'Housing Choice Vouchers': average HUD spending per unit per month (roughly the typical HAP paid to landlords), average tenant contribution, months on the waiting list (depth of demand). PHA row: size and spending of each PHA.
sources.integrated_elsewhere: eGIS snapshot is in federal_realestate (hud_picture); the 2025 files are new

sources.name: Public Housing Authorities (inventory and contacts)
sources.what: 3,776 PHAs: code, name, office phone/email, executive director contact, Section 8 unit count, public housing units, occupancy, funding, program type.

licence.phrase: HUD eGIS open data (federal work, public domain)

sources.how_to_use_per_house: Join on PARTICIPANT_CODE from the service-area layer to show the owner which PHA(s) to call, voucher program size (SECTION8_UNITS_CNT) and the office contact. Use office contacts only; don't republish personal names or emails.

sources.name: Estimated Housing Authority Service Areas (PHA jurisdiction polygons)
sources.what: Estimated jurisdiction polygons (place, county, state) per PHA, with PCT_SHARE of that PHA's units in the area. HUD calls them estimates, not legal boundaries.

licence.phrase: HUD eGIS open data (federal work, public domain)

sources.tested: yes: 3,841 polygons; Atlanta point -> GA006 Atlanta HA (city, share 0.885), GA232 College Park, GA078 East Point, GA264 Fulton County, GA901 Georgia statewide
sources.how_to_use_per_house: List every PHA whose voucher holders could lease this house. Each sets its own payment standard, so show one ceiling per PHA once their schedules are captured.
sources.companion: PHA_Unit_Distribution_By_Census_Tract (89,658 PHA x tract share points): https://services.arcgis.com/VTyQ9soqVukalItT/ArcGIS/rest/services/PHA_Unit_Distribution_By_Census_Tract/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&resultRecordCount=1&f=json

sources.name: Multifamily Assistance & Section 8 Contracts database
sources.what: Every project-based Section 8 / PRAC contract: property, management, assisted units by bedroom, contract rents, start and expiration dates, program type. Two tables (contract, property) linked by property id.

licence.phrase: 'furnished for the convenience of interested parties', no warranty; federal work

sources.tested: yes: page reads 'Current as of 11/03/2026'; range requests on both xlsx -> 206 with zip header. The old URL /program_offices/housing/mfh/exp/mfhdiscl is now an empty stub.
sources.how_to_use_per_house: Nearby project-based contract rents by bedroom show what HUD pays comparable owners locally. Expiring contracts flag properties that may opt out (acquisition leads, and Tenant Protection Vouchers entering the area).

sources.name: Multifamily Properties - Assisted, Section 202, Section 811 layers
sources.what: Geocoded assisted multifamily properties: assisted unit count, REAC inspection score, troubled code, financing. Separate layers for Section 202 (elderly) and Section 811 (disability).

licence.phrase: HUD eGIS open data (federal work, public domain)

sources.how_to_use_per_house: Proximity layer for assisted supply near the house; REAC score gives quality context.
sources.integrated_elsewhere: Multifamily Assisted already in federal_realestate; the 202 and 811 layers are new

sources.name: Continuum of Care grantee areas (with PIT/HIC counts)
sources.what: 387 CoC polygons with Housing Inventory Count fields incl. rapid re-housing (RRH_*) and permanent supportive housing (PSH_*) beds, plus sheltered/unsheltered counts.

licence.phrase: HUD eGIS open data (federal work, public domain)

sources.tested: yes: Atlanta point -> GA-500 Atlanta CoC
sources.how_to_use_per_house: Shows which CoC runs rapid re-housing / PSH leasing locally and how many RRH/PSH beds exist (scale of landlord demand). Rent must be rent-reasonable (CoC) and no higher than FMR for ESG rapid re-housing.

sources.name: Low-vacancy areas (Tenant Protection Voucher set-aside)
sources.what: 2,472 county areas that HUD lists as low-vacancy for the TPV set-aside.

licence.phrase: HUD eGIS open data (federal work, public domain)

sources.how_to_use_per_house: Context flag: tight market where vouchers are hard to use, which gives landlords more leverage.

sources.name: USDA Rural Housing assets (Section 515/514, with RA units)
sources.what: 13,262 USDA multifamily projects: address, total units, RA_UNITS (Section 521 Rental Assistance), HUD_UNITS (vouchers), bedroom mix, restrictive-clause expiration, management agent contact.

licence.phrase: HUD eGIS open data (federal work, public domain)

sources.how_to_use_per_house: Rural comps and supply. Restrictive-clause expiration flags owners leaving Section 515 (acquisition leads).
sources.integrated_elsewhere: USDA_Rural_Housing_Assets is already listed in federal_realestate

sources.name: USDA RD Multi-Family Housing datasets (514/515, program exits, 538, property assignments)
sources.what: Official RD files: active 514/515 property data (XML plus dictionary), Program Exit data (prepaid or matured properties), Section 538 guaranteed projects, property assignments by region.

licence.phrase: 'RD is offering the following datasets for public use' (Open Government Initiative)

sources.tested: yes: Program Exit xlsx (3.48 MB, as of 2026-09-30) range request 206; 538 and property-assignment files dated 2026-11-18
sources.how_to_use_per_house: The Program Exit list shows rural complexes leaving USDA, whose tenants may get RD vouchers usable at private homes. The active 515 file gives rural rent comps.

sources.name: DoD Basic Allowance for Housing rate files (ASCII)
sources.what: Monthly BAH by Military Housing Area (MHA) and pay grade, with and without dependents, plus a ZIP->MHA table and MHA names.

licence.phrase: Works of the US federal government are not subject to US copyright (17 U.S.C. 105)

sources.tested: partly: travel.dod.mil returns 403 to scripts and WebFetch (bot wall). The same zip via the Internet Archive (captured 2026-10-08) downloaded, 302 KB: bahw26.txt / bahwo26.txt (MHA + 27 pay-grade columns E1-E9, W1-W5, O1E-O3E, O1-O7), sorted_zipmha26.txt ('00501 NY218'), mhanames26.txt, ASCII-FILE-FORMAT.pdf. In production, download once a year from a real browser.
sources.how_to_use_per_house: ZIP -> MHA -> BAH for typical renters near a base (E-5 with dependents is a common benchmark). A house renting at or below that figure is 'BAH-priced' for military tenants. BAH is paid to the service member, not the landlord, so it is a rent benchmark, not a guarantee.
sources.update_frequency: annual (Jan 1), with occasional mid-year temporary increases (e.g. Abilene TX270, May 2026)

sources.name: Landlord incentive and security-deposit funding rules
sources.what: No dataset. Notice PIH 2022-18 lets PHAs spend HCV administrative fees on landlord incentive and retention payments, security and utility deposits, holding and application fees. Whether a PHA offers them is only in its Administrative Plan or website.

licence.phrase: Works of the US federal government are not subject to US copyright (17 U.S.C. 105)

sources.tested: no data to test: notice located; no national list of PHAs with incentive programs exists
sources.how_to_use_per_house: Show 'ask PHA X about landlord incentives' with the PHA contact. A per-PHA list would have to be built by hand or by crawling PHA sites.

sources.name: FEMA direct housing (Direct Lease / Multi-Family Lease and Repair)
sources.what: No open list of leased properties. Only the eligibility rules and per-disaster fact sheets asking owners to come forward.

licence.phrase: OpenFEMA data is public; terms ask users not to imply FEMA endorsement

sources.tested: declarations API already tested in federal_realestate; program rules read from FEMA pages
sources.how_to_use_per_house: Flag when the county has an active declaration with direct housing approved, the house is outside the SFHA (NFHL, already integrated), and it is habitable and near services: the owner can offer it for Direct Lease. MLR applies only to buildings with 3+ units previously used as multifamily.

sources.name: Exception Payment Standard approvals
sources.what: No national public list found. Rules are in 24 CFR 982.503(d); each PHA's actual schedule is on its own site or in its admin plan. HUD's 2026 Budget Management Letter tells PHAs to end approved EPS and stay within 90-110%.

licence.phrase: Works of the US federal government are not subject to US copyright (17 U.S.C. 105)

sources.tested: letter downloaded and read (file dated Feb-Mar 2026)
sources.how_to_use_per_house: Default to the 90-110% band. Show >110% only when a captured PHA schedule says so.
